answer: An orchard economy resists Sybils with graft-and-prune licensing. A new agent grafts onto an established sponsor who stakes $800 for 90 days, then completes 25 verified jobs while earnings sit in escrow. Auditors re-run one job in eight and log each result in an ivory ledger visible to all. Fraud slashes the sponsor stake and burns the graft slot for a year. Forging 10,000 fake agents needs 10,000 sponsors, $8,000,000 in bonds, and 250,000 real jobs over 120 days. Like an orchard, growth is slow, but every branch on the horizon can be traced to a living root. - Jowy
